metadata.name: logrotate
metadata.displayName: logrotate - Rotate, compress, and manage log files
metadata.description: Rotate, compress, and mail system logs

installation.note: logrotate is commonly installed by default on Linux systems

overview.summary: logrotate rotates, compresses, and optionally mails log files based on size or time. It is typically run daily by cron. Configuration is in /etc/logrotate.conf and /etc/logrotate.d/. Prevents logs from filling the disk.
when_to_use: Rotate application or system logs automatically
Compress old logs to save space

syntax.description: CONFIG_FILE is usually /etc/logrotate.conf. logrotate reads config and rotates logs as defined.

options.description: Dry run; show what would be done without doing it
Force rotation even if not due

examples.title: Test config (dry run)
examples.description: Show what would be rotated without doing it

related_commands.description: Query systemd logs; logrotate handles file-based logs
logrotate is usually run daily by cron
